precepts.text: I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left: the right hand angels go forth for righteousness, and the ones on the left go forth for judgment. A spirit stood before the Lord and said, I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets; and the Lord said, Thou shalt persuade him, and prevail also: go forth, and do so. God gave him the authority, the same way he gave Satan the authority in Job 1.
precepts.point: What is Satan's job? To tempt us, and he is only allowed to do what God allows. God gave him the authority over all that Job had, but said, upon himself put not forth thine hand.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
In Job, “the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them. And the Lord said unto Satan, Whence comest thou?” But I thought he got kicked out of heaven and was one of the fallen ones? No. He is there because he works for God. God created good angels and bad angels, and Satan’s job is to tempt us; he is only allowed to do what God allows. The prophet Micaiah saw the same court of heaven.

“I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left.” The angels on the right hand go forth for righteousness, and the ones on the left go forth for evil, for judgment.

“And the Lord said, Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth–gilead?” One said one thing and another said another. “And there came forth a spirit, and stood before the Lord, and said, I will persuade him.” “I will go forth, and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said, Thou shalt persuade him, and prevail also: go forth, and do so.”

God gave that spirit the authority to do it, the same way he gave Satan the authority in Job 1 to tempt Job: destroy everything, but do not touch Job himself. Even the lying spirit stands before the throne and goes out only when the Lord sends it. That is why the fallen angel doctrine is crap, and why it is a shame to hear black pastors, not only Edomite pastors, repeating that same garbage rhetoric and defiling the minds of the people.

precepts.text: The Lord holds council with His angels; that is the inquisition made into the counsels of the ungodly.
precepts.point: Many speak evil against leadership because they do not like when judgment comes out; a problem with the leadership the Most High set up is a problem with the Most High Himself.

note.label: Numbers 11: Beware of Murmuring

precepts.why:
The Lord “heard it” when the people complained, because nothing spoken is hidden from Him. Inquisition is made into the counsels of the ungodly, by the Lord and His angels, and here is that council.

“And the Lord said, Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth–gilead? And one said on this manner, and another said on that manner.” The Lord holds council with His angels over the deeds of men; that is the inquisition made into the counsels of the ungodly.

So when the people complained in the uttermost parts of the camp, the sound of their words came unto the Lord, and His anger was kindled, and the fire of the Lord burnt among them.

precepts.text: The same way the Lord put a lying spirit in the mouth of all Ahab's prophets, that he should go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead.
precepts.point: The reason is given: that the cruelty done to the threescore and ten sons of Jerubbaal might come, and their blood be laid upon Abimelech their brother, which slew them, and upon the men of Shechem, which aided him in the killing of his brethren. The hired men and the backers carried the blood guilt too. Abimelech ran for three years and everything looked good, but you are not getting away with evil.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

precepts.why:
The Lord sending an evil spirit between Abimelech and Shechem is the same way he dealt with Ahab. The spirit said, “I will go forth, and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said, Thou shalt persuade him, and prevail also: go forth, and do so.” Then Micaiah told the king, “Now therefore, behold, the Lord hath put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these thy prophets, and the Lord hath spoken evil concerning thee.”

The Lord put a lying spirit in the mouth of all Ahab's prophets, that he should go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead. He put an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem, that the cruelty done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might come back on him and on those who aided him. Abimelech ran for three years and everything looked good, but you are not getting away with evil.

precepts.text: Elisha tells a later king of Israel to go to the prophets of his father and his mother, showing how a true prophet of the Most High kept his distance from the corrupted worship of the northern kingdom.
precepts.point: This is the setting for a division that ran between the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom. After the split, the northern kingdom fell into idolatry and forsook the Levites, so a prophet of the Most High would want nothing to do with their manner of worship.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

precepts.why:
“And Elisha said unto the king of Israel, What have I to do with thee? get thee to the prophets of thy father, and to the prophets of thy mother.”

After the kingdom split, the northern kingdom fell into idolatry, so a true prophet of the Most High kept his distance from its corrupted worship. Elisha told a later king of Israel to go to the prophets of his father and his mother; he wanted nothing to do with their manner of worship.

That is the setting in 1 Kings 22. Ahab gathered “about four hundred men” as his prophets, and they said with one mouth, “Go up; for the Lord shall deliver it into the hand of the king.” These were the prophets of the northern kingdom, not the prophets of the Most High.

precepts.text: Jeroboam cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and made priests after the manner of the nations, so that any man could consecrate himself to serve gods that are no gods.
precepts.point: This is the setting for a division that ran between the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom. After the split, the northern kingdom fell into idolatry and forsook the Levites, so a prophet of the Most High would want nothing to do with their manner of worship.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

precepts.why:
“Have ye not cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and have made you priests after the manner of the nations of other lands? so that whosoever cometh to consecrate himself with a young bullock and seven rams, the same may be a priest of them that are no gods.”

Jeroboam cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and forsook the Levites. He made priests after the manner of the nations, so that any man could consecrate himself to serve gods that are no gods. That is the division that ran between the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom, and it is why the four hundred prophets Ahab gathered could not be trusted, even though Jehoshaphat said, “I am as thou art, my people as thy people, my horses as thy horses.”

precepts.text: Amaziah the priest of Bethel tries to drive the prophet Amos out of the king's chapel, telling him to prophesy in Judah instead, which shows how the northern kingdom rejected the true word.
precepts.point: This is the setting for a division that ran between the northern kingdom and the southern kingdom. After the split, the northern kingdom fell into idolatry and forsook the Levites, so a prophet of the Most High would want nothing to do with their manner of worship.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

precepts.why:
“Then Amaziah the priest of Beth–el sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, Amos hath conspired against thee in the midst of the house of Israel: the land is not able to bear all his words.” Amos had said, “Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away captive out of their own land.”

So Amaziah told the prophet, “O thou seer, go, flee thee away into the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and prophesy there: But prophesy not again any more at Beth–el: for it is the king’s chapel, and it is the king’s court.” The priest of Bethel drove the prophet out of the king’s chapel.

That shows how the northern kingdom rejected the true word. The king’s chapel had its own priests and its own prophets, and the word of the Most High was not welcome there; which is why Ahab could gather four hundred prophets who all said the same thing.

precepts.text: With the Most High is strength and wisdom, and the deceived and the deceiver are his, for he leadeth counsellors away spoiled and maketh the judges fools.
precepts.point: The Most High put a lying spirit in the mouth of these prophets and spoke evil concerning Ahab. The deceiver as well as the deceived are under the hand of the Most High, who uses the lie to bring the judgment he has already declared.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

precepts.why:
“With him is strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver are his.” He leadeth counsellors away spoiled and maketh the judges fools.

Micaiah saw “the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left.” The Lord asked, “Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth–gilead?” A spirit came forth and said, “I will go forth, and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said, Thou shalt persuade him, and prevail also: go forth, and do so.”

“Now therefore, behold, the Lord hath put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these thy prophets, and the Lord hath spoken evil concerning thee.” The deceiver as well as the deceived are under the hand of the Most High. He used the lie of the four hundred prophets to bring on Ahab the judgment he had already declared.

precepts.text: David charges the princes of Israel, saying the Lord has given the inhabitants of the land into his hand and the land is subdued before the Lord, which is why Edom had no king of its own in Jehoshaphat's day.
precepts.point: Jehoshaphat makes peace with the king of Israel and puts the remnant of the sodomites out of the land. There is then no king in Edom but a deputy, because Edom had been subdued and had not yet revolted.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

precepts.why:
David charged the princes of Israel to help Solomon, saying, “Is not the Lord your God with you? and hath he not given you rest on every side? for he hath given the inhabitants of the land into mine hand; and the land is subdued before the Lord, and before his people.”

The Most High gave the inhabitants of the land into David’s hand, and the land was subdued. That is why, in Jehoshaphat’s day, “There was then no king in Edom: a deputy was king.” Edom had been subdued and had not yet revolted, so it had no king of its own.

precepts.text: The Most High put a lying spirit in the mouth of Ahab's prophets to draw him to his fall; the king who trusts false counsel over the true prophet is set up for destruction.
precepts.point: The Most High sent a prophet who asked why he sought after gods that could not even deliver their own people out of his hand. This is why counsel is important. The prophet was trying to counsel Amaziah to destroy the idols, and instead Amaziah threatened him and told him to forbear, be quiet. The prophet forbore, but said the Most High had determined to destroy him because he had done this and had not hearkened to counsel.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 25: Amaziah Serves the Most High With a Divided Heart

precepts.why:
“And the Lord said, Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth–gilead?” A spirit came forth and said, “I will go forth, and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.” And the Lord said, “Thou shalt persuade him, and prevail also: go forth, and do so.” The Most High put a lying spirit in the mouth of Ahab’s prophets to draw him to his fall.

The king who trusts false counsel over the true prophet is set up for destruction. That is Amaziah. The Most High gave him the victory over the children of Seir, and he responded by grabbing the idols of the people he had just defeated: he “brought the gods of the children of Seir, and set them up to be his gods, and bowed down himself before them, and burned incense unto them.” That is the divided heart in action.

This is why counsel is important. The prophet asked him, “Why hast thou sought after the gods of the people, which could not deliver their own people out of thine hand?” He was trying to counsel Amaziah to destroy the idols, and instead Amaziah threatened him: “Art thou made of the king’s counsel? forbear; why shouldest thou be smitten?” Be quiet. The prophet forbore, but said, “I know that God hath determined to destroy thee, because thou hast done this, and hast not hearkened unto my counsel.”

points: There is yet one man, Micaiah, by whom we may inquire of the Lord: so it's being known here that this man is a prophet. They're acknowledging that the spirit of the Lord is on this man; if you want to inquire anything of God, you must go to this man. But I hate him. Although the spirit of the Lord is on this man, I hate his stinking guts.

He does not prophesy good concerning me: he don't prophesy multiple wives. He don't prophesy you don't got to wear fringes on your clothes. He's prophesying that you do got to keep the laws of the Sabbath. He's telling you you got to have fringes on all your garments. He's telling you one wife as it pertains to the Bible. We don't like that. We hate you for that. Oh, you have one wife? Okay, you're gay. So I guess Paul was a battyman. I guess Christ was a battyman. They weren't married. What do you have to say about that?

Now, they put him in prison because they did not like what he prophesied, what he spoke. These weren't actions. They didn't hate this brother because he committed adultery with a brother's wife, or he hit a brother, or he stole from a brother. They hated him because the words of the laws that came out of his mouth, they did not like it. Micaiah's light shined on their darkness, and roaches are revealed when the light turns on. That's why they hate the way they hate. So they fed him the bread of affliction and the water of affliction.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

points: After three years without war between Syria and Israel, Jehoshaphat king of Judah comes down to the king of Israel. Ahab reminds his servants that Ramoth in Gilead belongs to Israel, yet they sit still and do not take it out of the hand of the king of Syria.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: Ahab asks Jehoshaphat to go with him to battle, and Jehoshaphat answers that he is as Ahab is, his people and horses as Ahab's, but first asks that they inquire at the word of the Lord. Ahab gathers about four hundred prophets, who all say with one mouth, go up, for the Lord shall deliver it into the hand of the king.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: Jehoshaphat is not moved by four hundred prophets speaking the same thing, and asks whether there is not yet a prophet of the Lord that they may inquire of him. He wants to hear from a true prophet of the Most High, not from prophets who serve the king.

Ahab answers that there is one man, Micaiah the son of Imlah, but he hates him because Micaiah does not prophesy good concerning him, but evil. Jehoshaphat rebukes him, saying, let not the king say so.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: The king of Israel calls an officer to hasten Micaiah, while Ahab and Jehoshaphat sit each on his throne in their robes at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets prophesy before them.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah makes horns of iron and says, thus saith the Lord, with these shalt thou push the Syrians until thou have consumed them. Here again a man claims to speak for the Most High while the whole company presses Ahab to go up and prosper.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: The messenger tells Micaiah that all the prophets declare good to the king with one mouth, and urges him to speak likewise. Micaiah answers that whatever the Lord saith unto him, that will he speak, and at first he echoes the others, prompting the king to adjure him to tell nothing but the truth.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: Micaiah then reveals what he saw, all Israel scattered on the hills as sheep having no shepherd, and the Lord saying these have no master. He saw the Lord on his throne with all the host of heaven, and a spirit that offered to be a lying spirit in the mouth of all Ahab's prophets to persuade him to fall at Ramoth-gilead.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: The Most High put a lying spirit in the mouth of these prophets and spoke evil concerning Ahab. The deceiver as well as the deceived are under the hand of the Most High, who uses the lie to bring the judgment he has already declared.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah smites Micaiah on the cheek and asks which way the spirit of the Lord went from him to speak to Micaiah, defending his own false prophecy. The king of Israel orders Micaiah taken back and put in prison, fed with bread and water of affliction until Ahab returns in peace.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: Micaiah answers that if Ahab returns at all in peace, the Lord has not spoken by him, and calls all the people to hearken. His word stands as the test of who truly spoke for the Most High.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat go up to Ramoth-gilead. Ahab disguises himself and tells Jehoshaphat to wear his robes, hoping to escape the word spoken against him, while the king of Syria commands his captains to fight only against the king of Israel.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: The captains pursue Jehoshaphat until they perceive he is not the king of Israel and turn back. A certain man draws a bow at a venture and smites Ahab between the joints of the harness, and the king is held up in his chariot until he dies at even, the blood running into the chariot.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: When they wash the chariot in the pool of Samaria, the dogs lick up his blood according to the word of the Lord. The judgment pronounced earlier against Ahab and his house begins to be fulfilled exactly as spoken.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: The rest of the acts of Ahab, the ivory house he made and the cities he built, are written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel. Ahab sleeps with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigns in his stead.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: Jehoshaphat the son of Asa begins to reign over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab, at thirty-five years old, and reigns twenty-five years in Jerusalem. He walks in the ways of Asa his father, doing right in the eyes of the Lord, though the high places are not taken away and the people still burn incense there.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: Jehoshaphat makes peace with the king of Israel and puts the remnant of the sodomites out of the land. There is then no king in Edom but a deputy, because Edom had been subdued and had not yet revolted.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: Ahaziah the son of Ahab begins to reign over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat and reigns two years. He does evil in the sight of the Lord and walks in the way of his father and his mother and in the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.

note.label: 1 Kings 22: A Lying Spirit and the Fall of Ahab

points: He serves Baal and worships him and provokes the Lord God of Israel to anger, according to all that his father had done. The sin of the house of Ahab continues into the next generation.
